definitions.gloss: (of food or drink) to suit one's taste; to be to one's liking
definitions.explanation: Said of food or drink that one finds tasty; literally 'to fit the mouth.' The honorific お{口|くち}に{合|あ}う is the standard way to ask a guest whether the food is to their liking, and お{口|くち}に{合|あ}うかどうか{分|わ}かりませんが is the modest formula when serving.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{料理|りょうり}→料理：01523_ryouri⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{口|くち}に{合|あ}う。
お{口|くち}に{合|あ}う⟦かどうか→かどうか：28299_kadouka⟧⟦{分|わ}かりません→分かる：00463_wakaru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦どうぞ→どうぞ：02920_douzo⟧。
examples.english: I'm not sure it will be to your liking, but please have some.

examples.japanese: ⟦{留学|りゅうがく}→留学：03677_ryuugaku⟧⟦{中|ちゅう}→〜中：09840_chuu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{食事|しょくじ}→食事：02087_shokuji⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{口|くち}に{合|あ}わなくて、⟦{母|はは}→母：00549_haha⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{料理|りょうり}→料理：01523_ryouri⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{恋|こい}しかった→恋しい：03055_koishii⟧。
examples.english: While studying abroad the food didn't suit me, and I missed my mother's cooking.

notes:
Literally 'to fit the mouth': food or drink matches one's taste.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- お{口|くち}に{合|あ}いました⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧: Did you like it? (to a guest)
- お{口|くち}に{合|あ}う⟦かどうか→かどうか：28299_kadouka⟧: whether it will be to your liking
- {口|くち}に{合|あ}わない: not to one's taste

USAGE:
The honorific お{口|くち}に{合|あ}う is host language, part of the ritual of serving food modestly. Between friends the plain form is normal.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- おいしい: delicious — describes the food itself, not its match with the eater
- ⟦{好|この}み→好み：02767_konomi⟧: preference — the noun for one's taste in general
